items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: I was just listening to a couple of Chet Baker records recorded in Italy

ctx.x: It’s a good feeling isn’t it, but when I said why did he say that about the bass, do you think the bass is — this was a question for later but I’m going to try it now. Music has changed the way it’s produced so much over the years, and I’m wondering if the bass has been somewhat immune from all the changes in technology?

Well it’s been affected by pick-ups and, you know the high-tech method of recording to a certain extent. I was just listening to a couple of Chet Baker records recorded in Italy with these bizarre mixes and it sounded like they were just recording the bass through a pick-up that sounded like a banjo you know. But the bass has not changed. I have a bass that’s 280 years old, one of my basses, and it’s got the same — the sound improves year by year by aging. And a contractor called me up recently about a show that…

When you came up here in 2005 to play with Kenny — and I recall that you didn’t want an amplifier, the room was acoustically really wonderful, but do you find that your fellow musicians on a club date or something play differently volume-wise when you don’t have an amplifier? Are they sympathetic to your bass set-up?
